builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Soraka: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (3,097 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 61.3% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A recovery-focused enchanter who must land Q to sustain herself and reduce the cost of repeated ally heals, while silence denies enemy casts. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Moonstone Renewer → Redemption → Dawncore. Summon Aery keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Dream Maker, Mikael's Blessing.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Moonstone Renewer → Redemption → Dawncore, with Summon Aery.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Moonstone Renewer → Redemption → Dawncore) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 61.3% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Moonstone Renewer → Redemption → Dawncore.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula: Soraka creates a starfield that deals [70 / 95 / 120 / 145 / 170 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage to champions. The field lingers for [1.5] seconds, Silencing enemies inside. When the zone disappears, champions inside the zone are Rooted for [1 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 1.75 / 2] second(s) and take [70 / 95 / 120 / 145 / 170 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage.

Soraka calls down a star, dealing [85 / 120 / 155 / 190 / 225 + (0.35) × AP] magic damage and Slowing by [30]% for [1.5] seconds. 

Hitting an enemy champion grants Soraka Rejuvenation, which restores [60 / 75 / 90 / 105 / 120 + (0.3) × AP] Health over [2.5] seconds and grants [(0.2 / 0.225 / 0.25 / 0.275 / 0.3) × 100]% Move Speed decaying over the same duration.
Soraka gains [90]% Move Speed while moving towards allied champions who are below [40]% Health.

Soraka calls upon divine powers, restoring [150 / 250 / 350 + (0.5) × AP] Health to all allied champions, regardless of distance. Healing is increased to [(150 / 250 / 350 + (0.5) × AP) × ((1 + 0.5))] on targets below 40% Health.

Soraka restores [90 / 110 / 130 / 150 / 170 + (0.5) × AP] Health to another allied champion.

If Soraka is affected by Rejuvenation, the Health cost will be reduced by [(0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 1) × 100]%, and the target will gain Rejuvenation for @Spell.SorakaQ:HoTDuration@ seconds.

builds.name: Starcall funded rescue
builds.summary: Test whether Q contact and out-of-combat reset can fund repeated low-cost W casts.
builds.goal: Test whether Q contact and out-of-combat reset can fund repeated low-cost W casts.
builds.hypothesis: Q grants Rejuvenation healing and movement; W health cost is reduced by 80-100% while Rejuvenation is active and transfers it to the ally. Warmog supplies an out-of-combat reset only after 2000 bonus health; Visage enhances Soraka own Q recovery. Moonstone and Redemption support ally rescue while the quest remains retained.
testPlan: Required state: Confirm actual bonus-health threshold, eight seconds without damage for Warmog, and Q before W.
Log W health cost with/without Rejuvenation and Warmog activation at actual observed bonus health.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Burst or constant damage prevents the reset; missed Q spends health at full cost.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Warmog is not in-combat regeneration and its threshold is not presumed satisfied.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Celestial Opposition, Warmog's Armor, Spirit Visage, Moonstone Renewer, Redemption, Boots of Swiftness. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Tempo and pursuit
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Soraka: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A recovery-focused enchanter who must land Q to sustain herself and reduce the cost of repeated ally heals, while silence denies enemy casts. Measure Q hits, self-health cost and ally heal availability. AP damage does not justify starving repeated W heals; silence placement and healing reduction need separate tests. Movement tools and compatible control marks test coordinated pursuit or escape.
builds.summary: Movement tools and compatible control marks test coordinated pursuit or escape.
testPlan: Kit question for Soraka: Measure Q hits, self-health cost and ally heal availability. AP damage does not justify starving repeated W heals; silence placement and healing reduction need separate tests.

Start with the early core (Support quest, Shurelya or Mandate according to the kit) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use real support income and keep the quest/vision slot.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Movement tools and compatible control marks test coordinated pursuit or escape. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: A star falls from the sky at the target location dealing magic damage and slowing enemies. If an enemy champion is hit by Starcall, Soraka recovers Health. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Mandate needs eligible control and allied follow-up; speed is not guaranteed damage.

The route fails Soraka's stated kit question: Measure Q hits, self-health cost and ally heal availability. AP damage does not justify starving repeated W heals; silence placement and healing reduction need separate tests.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility. Also record allies lost while spending on personal damage.
tradeoffs: Mandate needs eligible control and allied follow-up; speed is not guaranteed damage.
Full cost 10,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Support quest, Shurelya or Mandate according to the kit. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Begin with the actual support quest item; Celestial Opposition is earned by transformation, not directly bought as a 400-gold legendary. Keep buying vision.
Imperial Mandate, Redemption, Mikael's Blessing are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Equinox artillery escort
builds.summary: Use AP to threaten both Equinox hits while improving low-health Wish rescue.
builds.goal: Use AP to threaten both Equinox hits while improving low-health Wish rescue.
builds.hypothesis: E deals 0.4 AP magic damage on placement and again on its delayed root; Q slow helps hold the zone. R has 0.5 AP healing increased by half on allies below 40%. Cryptbloom can add a takedown heal and Mandate needs the E root, while Staff/Helia turn successful offensive contact into ally support.
testPlan: Required state: Target stays in E for 1.5 seconds; Q and healing recipients are available.
Measure E first hit, root/second hit, Mandate mark and subsequent Helia heal/Wish.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Silence alone does not root; delaying healing to fish for damage loses allies.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Silence is not the immobilization required for current Mandate.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Celestial Opposition, Imperial Mandate, Echoes of Helia, Staff of Flowing Water, Cryptbloom, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
